segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.ko: 부엌에서 바쁘게 움직이는 걸 걱정할 필요가 없었으니까요. 네, 좋았습니다. 그렇게 즐거운 추석 점심을 먹었습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: We actually ate just sort of a later lunch together. And as we were eating, my father-in-law mentioned how he's been doing a lot of hiking recently.
segments.ko: 사실 좀 늦은 점심을 같이 먹었죠. 식사를 하면서 장인어른께서 최근에 등산을 많이 하셨다고 말씀하셨어요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And how he found this great chestnut spot in the woods and how he's been going to the woods and collecting chestnuts and picking up chestnuts and it was chestnut season while he was talking about that and acorns as well.
segments.ko: 숲에서 아주 좋은 밤나무 명당을 발견하셨고 숲에 가서 밤을 줍고 계신다면서요. 밤과 도토리 철이라는 말씀도 하셨죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And so he was asking me about in Canada, do we eat chestnuts and do we collect chestnuts? And we do have chestnuts in Kelowna.
segments.ko: 그러면서 캐나다에서도 밤을 먹는지, 밤을 줍는지 물어보시더라고요. 켈로나에도 밤이 있긴 해요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: I remember seeing them as I was growing up from time to time, but we don't really eat chestnuts. And at least not my family and my friends, I don't think eat chestnuts really either.
segments.ko: 자라면서 가끔 본 기억은 나지만, 우린 밤을 잘 먹지 않거든요. 적어도 제 가족이나 친구들은 밤을 먹지 않는 것 같아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So he was a little bit shocked at this like, oh, you don't eat chestnuts, you haven't collected chestnuts.
segments.ko: 그래서 장인어른은 "오, 밤을 안 먹어? 밤을 주워본 적도 없어?" 하시며 좀 놀라셨죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And so he asked me and the other family members, and if after our meal, if we wanted to go to this spot in the woods and go and collect some chestnuts, it was a beautiful day.
segments.ko: 그래서 식사 후에 저와 다른 가족들에게 숲에 있는 그 명소에 가서 밤을 좀 줍고 싶은지 물어보셨어요. 날씨가 아주 좋았습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: We've had a lovely fall here in Korea. The weather's been really, in my opinion, a little bit too hot.
segments.ko: 올해 한국의 가을은 정말 아름다웠어요. 제 생각엔 날씨가 좀 지나치게 덥긴 했지만요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: It's finally cooling down to like regular fall temperature, but a few weeks ago still, it was very warm and just really, really pleasant.
segments.ko: 이제야 평년 가을 기온으로 시원해지고 있지만, 몇 주 전만 해도 여전히 매우 따뜻하고 정말 기분이 좋았습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: We've had beautiful blue skies and sunny days recently, and the Chuseok day was just like that. It was one of those days.
segments.ko: 최근에 아름다운 파란 하늘과 화창한 날들이 이어졌는데, 추석 당일도 딱 그랬습니다. 그런 날 중 하나였죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So after we finished the meal, we decided, yeah, let's do it. Let's take advantage of this nice weather.
segments.ko: 그래서 식사를 마친 후, 그러자고 결정했습니다. 이 좋은 날씨를 만끽해 보자고 말이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: Let's go walk for a bit and burn off some of the calories from the pizza and go and collect some chestnuts. And so that's what we did.
segments.ko: 좀 걷기도 하고 피자로 섭취한 칼로리도 태울 겸 밤을 주우러 가기로 했습니다. 그래서 그렇게 했죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: My father-in-law loaded us up into his vehicle and he drove us to his secret chestnut spot which was on the side of a highway like this really busy highway.
segments.ko: 장인어른께서 차에 우리를 태우고 아주 붐비는 고속도로 옆에 있는 장인어른만의 비밀 밤나무 장소로 데려다 주셨습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: He just kind of like pulled off and he's like we got to go up here. And I was like are you sure is this okay?
segments.ko: 장인어른이 차를 세우시더니 "여기로 올라가야 해"라고 하셨어요. 전 "정말요? 여기 괜찮은 건가요?"라고 생각했죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: But just a little bit off of the highway there was a hiking path and then you know Korea is very it's extremely mountainous.
segments.ko: 하지만 고속도로에서 조금만 벗어나니 등산로가 있었고, 아시다시피 한국은 산이 정말 많잖아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: In fact, I think 80% of the Korean peninsula is covered in mountains from what I've heard before. So it's not very frequent that you go into the forest and it's just flat.
segments.ko: 사실 제가 듣기로는 한반도의 80%가 산으로 덮여 있다고 해요. 그래서 숲에 들어갔을 때 그냥 평지인 경우는 거의 없습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: You're always hiking up somewhere or going down some hill. This is just life in Korea. It's like going uphill or going downhill.
segments.ko: 항상 어딘가로 올라가거나 내려가고 있죠. 이게 한국에서의 삶입니다. 언덕을 오르거나 내리는 식이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So immediately we are just hiking up this mountain and there were the four of us, my father-in-law, my mother-in-law, my wife, and me as well.
segments.ko: 그래서 곧바로 산을 오르기 시작했고 장인어른, 장모님, 아내, 그리고 저까지 네 명이 함께했습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And yeah, we hiked for 10 minutes or so just up this hill, and then he said, here we are in the chestnut hunting spot, and he was right on the money.
segments.ko: 10분 정도 언덕을 올라가니 장인어른이 "여기가 밤 따는 곳이야"라고 하셨는데, 정확했습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: There were chestnuts all over the place. They were falling down as we were collecting them off the ground.
segments.ko: 사방에 밤이 널려 있었습니다. 바닥에 있는 걸 줍는 동안에도 밤이 툭툭 떨어지고 있었죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And this was my first time collecting chestnuts, so I was a complete newbie, but my father-in-law instructed me,
segments.ko: 저는 밤을 줍는 게 처음이라 완전 초보였는데, 장인어른께서 가르쳐 주셨어요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And he even gave me this special stick that was sitting right by the side of the road so I imagine that he had found it earlier and then used it for collecting the chestnuts.
segments.ko: 길가에 놓여 있던 특수한 막대기도 주셨는데 장인어른이 미리 찾아두고 밤을 줍는 데 사용하셨던 것 같아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: But it was this long stick and it had a kind of forked ending almost like an inverted slingshot if you know what a slingshot is.
segments.ko: 긴 막대기였는데 끝이 갈라져 있어서 마치 뒤집힌 새총 같았습니다. 새총이 뭔지 아신다면요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: It's like one of those Y shaped devices that you can use to shoot rocks, right, with an elastic band, some kind of an elastic band to propel the rocks forward.
segments.ko: 고무줄 같은 걸로 돌을 앞으로 쏘아 올리는 Y자 모양의 장치 말이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So it was almost like that. It was like this inverted slingshot shape.
segments.ko: 거의 그런 모양이었어요. 뒤집힌 새총 모양이었죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And what you could do with that stick is quickly when you would find the chestnut on the ground, of course, a chestnut comes in this protective shell that is really, really spiky and very, very prickly.
segments.ko: 그 막대기로 할 수 있는 건 바닥에서 밤을 발견했을 때, 아시다시피 밤은 아주 아주 가시가 돋친 따가운 껍질에 싸여 있잖아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And I wasn't aware of how prickly they were until I touched one. I picked one up because I'm a noob and I don't know better.
segments.ko: 직접 만져보기 전까지는 얼마나 따가운지 몰랐습니다. 제가 초보라 잘 몰라서 그냥 하나를 집어 들었거든요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: I was even wearing some gloves, but the spines on the chestnut went right through the glove. And I was like, oh, wow, very prickly, very, very painful to pick those up.
segments.ko: 장갑을 끼고 있었는데도 밤 가시가 장갑을 뚫고 들어오더라고요. '와, 정말 따갑네, 그냥 줍기엔 너무 아프다'라고 생각했죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So you do need to use this kind of stick. And he showed me the kind of chestnut that you want to look for.
segments.ko: 그래서 이런 막대기를 사용해야 합니다. 장인어른은 어떤 밤을 찾아야 하는지 보여주셨어요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: You want to find one where that protective prickly shell is kind of open a little bit, and then I could use the forks on the end of the stick to kind of pry that open, open it up,
segments.ko: 가시 껍질이 약간 벌어져 있는 걸 찾아야 해요. 그러면 막대기 끝의 갈라진 부분을 이용해 껍질을 벌려 열 수 있습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: and then the chestnut would pop out, and you could pick it up and collect it off of the forest floor.
segments.ko: 밤이 톡 튀어나오게 해서 숲 바닥에서 주울 수 있게 말이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And I had a plastic bag that he gave me as well that I tied to my belt buckle, so it was hanging from my pants.
segments.ko: 장인어른이 주신 비닐봉지도 벨트 고리에 묶어서 바지에 대롱대롱 매달았습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And then I could pick up the chestnuts and put them in the bag and just go around collecting as many chestnuts as I could. And yeah, we did that for like probably an hour or so.
segments.ko: 그러고 나서 밤을 주워 가방에 담으며 최대한 많이 모으러 다녔습니다. 한 시간 정도 그렇게 했던 것 같아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And it was just awesome. Just walking in the forest, very quiet, like I said, a lovely day and just picking up chestnuts.
segments.ko: 정말 좋았습니다. 숲속을 걷는 것도, 아주 조용한 것도, 말씀드린 대로 날씨도 화창한 날에 밤을 줍는 게 말이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And I guess as you tend to do in this kind of situation, we all started together. But then, you know, we're all looking at the forest floor and looking for chestnuts,
segments.ko: 이런 상황에서 으레 그렇듯 처음에는 다 같이 시작했습니다. 하지만 다들 숲 바닥을 보며 밤을 찾다 보니,
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: and they're all over the place, but some places had better deposits of chestnuts than others. And naturally, you kind of wander off a little bit away from each other.
segments.ko: 밤은 사방에 있지만 어떤 곳은 다른 곳보다 밤이 더 많이 몰려 있기도 하잖아요. 그러다 보니 자연스럽게 서로 조금씩 떨어져서 돌아다니게 되었습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And so I was kind of going in my own direction and my father-in-law and mother-in-law, what they were going in their own direction and my wife was going in her own direction.
segments.ko: 저는 제 방향대로 가고 장인어른과 장모님은 그분들대로, 아내는 또 아내대로 자기 길을 갔죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And eventually I kind of got separated from them a little bit and I was out on my own just in the middle of the forest and I found myself thinking like wow, this is such a cool hobby.
segments.ko: 결국 저는 가족들과 조금 떨어져서 숲 한가운데 혼자 있게 되었고, '와, 이거 정말 멋진 취미다'라고 생각하게 되었습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: This is such a cool activity to do I'm out here in the forest foraging and foraging just means collecting food looking for food hunting for food and collecting it.
segments.ko: 이건 정말 멋진 활동이에요. 숲에서 'foraging(수렵 채집)'을 하고 있는 거니까요. 'foraging'은 음식을 찾고 사냥하고 수집하는 것을 의미합니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: You wouldn't necessarily forage for an animal that's hunting, but if you're collecting mushrooms or chestnuts, berries, this kind of thing, this activity is foraging.
segments.ko: 동물을 사냥하는 것을 'foraging'이라고 하지는 않지만 버섯이나 밤, 베리류 같은 것을 채집한다면 그 활동이 바로 'foraging'입니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So I was just out there in the forest foraging for chestnuts and it was just so chill and relaxing and I was enjoying it.
segments.ko: 그래서 숲에서 밤을 채집하고 있었는데 정말 여유롭고 편안했습니다. 그 시간을 즐기고 있었죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And thinking about how it's awesome that nature is just providing us with these really healthy and delicious and organic chestnuts and just how awesome that is.
segments.ko: 자연이 우리에게 이렇게 건강하고 맛있고 유기농인 밤을 제공해 준다는 게 얼마나 멋진 일인지 생각하면서요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And I found myself reflecting and comparing hunting for chestnuts with running. Now these days I spend a lot of my free time running and running is awesome.
segments.ko: 그러다 문득 밤을 줍는 것과 달리기를 비교하며 되돌아보게 되었습니다. 요즘 전 여가 시간의 많은 부분을 달리며 보내고 있고 달리기는 정말 좋습니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: It gives me a lot of enjoyment in life. It's something that I really like doing. And if you're a regular Culips listener, you'll know that I enjoy running in marathons and doing a lot of running really.

segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: However, I get a lot of satisfaction from running. If you finish a race or break a personal record, it feels great, but it's really difficult.
segments.ko: 하지만 달리기를 통해 얻는 만족감은 큽니다. 경주를 마치거나 개인 기록을 경신하면 기분이 최고지만, 과정은 정말 힘들거든요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: Like while you're running, for me, maybe everybody else is different, but for me, I'm never really enjoying the running part of running.
segments.ko: 달리는 동안에는, 다른 사람들은 다를 수도 있겠지만 저는 달리는 행위 자체를 즐겨본 적이 없는 것 같아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: It's the after, the reward that you get from finishing running that feels good.
segments.ko: 달리고 난 후, 완주했을 때 얻는 보상이 기분 좋은 거죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: But most of the time that high that you get from running, and people call it a runner's high. For me, it's like when you finish, it's not while you're doing the activity.
segments.ko: 사람들이 '러너스 하이'라고 부르는 그 쾌감도 대부분의 경우 저에게는 활동 중에 오는 게 아니라 끝났을 때 찾아옵니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: While I'm doing running, it's tough and difficult and I don't really like it too much.
segments.ko: 달리는 동안에는 힘들고 괴로워서 사실 별로 좋아하지 않거든요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And then also a lot of times when I wake up in the morning or after a long run, I feel pretty tired and I have some little aches and pains.
segments.ko: 게다가 아침에 일어날 때나 장거리 달리기를 하고 나면 꽤 피곤하고 여기저기 잔통증이 있기도 합니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: If you're a regular runner running in your 40s who's trying to go fast, then probably you always have some little aches and pains.
segments.ko: 40대에 속도를 내려고 노력하는 평범한 러너라면 아마 늘 잔통증을 달고 살 겁니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: And so I was thinking about this like why am I doing this hobby? Why am I doing running so much? Like maybe I should just change to being a chestnut hunter.
segments.ko: 그래서 '내가 왜 이 취미를 하고 있지? 왜 이렇게 달리기를 많이 하는 걸까?'라는 생각이 들더라고요. '그냥 밤 사냥꾼으로 전향해야 하나?' 싶기도 했고요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: This is so much more chill. I'm out in the forest. I'm walking at a pace which is comfortable for me and it's just relaxing.
segments.ko: 이건 훨씬 더 여유롭잖아요. 숲에 나와서 나에게 편안한 속도로 걷고 있고, 그냥 편안하죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: No aches, no pains and I'm getting all of this delicious free organic food from the forest floor or nature's bounty.
segments.ko: 아픈 데도 없고 숲 바닥, 즉 대자연의 선물로부터 이 모든 맛있고 공짜인 유기농 음식을 얻고 있으니까요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So I don't know, maybe in the future, I'm still probably gonna continue running, but maybe I need to find some balance.
segments.ko: 모르겠어요, 미래에도 아마 달리기는 계속하겠지만 어느 정도 균형을 찾아야 할 것 같아요.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: It was kind of like a wake up call for me. Maybe I need to find some balance in my life, not go all in on running and spend some more time doing some relaxing activities in nature.
segments.ko: 저에게는 일종의 경종을 울리는 계기였습니다. 삶의 균형을 찾고 달리기에만 올인하지 말고 자연 속에서 여유로운 활동을 하며 시간을 더 보내야 할 것 같다는 생각 말이죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: Because I think going into nature like that, it's just really refreshing for me and I really, really enjoyed that.
segments.ko: 그렇게 자연 속으로 들어가는 것이 저에게는 정말 상쾌한 일이고, 그 시간을 정말 즐겼기 때문입니다.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So, to be honest, I wasn't on my own for too long. I was only wandering in the woods there, picking up chestnuts and reflecting on my life for maybe 10 or 15 minutes.
segments.ko: 솔직히 혼자 있었던 시간이 길지는 않았어요. 숲속을 거닐며 밤을 줍고 제 삶을 되돌아본 건 10분에서 15분 정도였죠.
segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: until my mother-in-law called me over and said, Hey Andrew, don't wander off on your own. Come back with us. So I went and rejoined them.

segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So I was really cautious making sure each chestnut was perfect before putting it in my bag. But I did collect about a kilogram and then yeah that was it for our chestnut collecting.

segments.en: not as nutty as like a peanut or a chestnut or anything like that, but kind of earthy, nutty, and actually quite delicious taste.

segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: So I was happy that we had all of these chestnuts. And one thing that I have had before from France, actually I believe one of my friends gave me some chestnut jam from France like a few years ago.

segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: more quickly than if you had to use a knife and kind of whittle all of the skin off. However, we only have one pair.

segments.speaker: Andrew

segments.en: My wife is like really nimble with her hands and I'm the opposite. I'm really clumsy with my hands.
